texts.preamble: Ved Prakash vs Vijay Laxmi on 2 May, 2018 In The Court Of Sh. Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler Additional District Judge-01 (Central) Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi. Cs No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash S/o Late Sh. Durga Prasad R/o B-178, Sector-44, Noida Uttar Pradesh Versus 1. Vijay Laxmi W/o Late Sh. Sushil Gupta 2. Chetan Gupta 3. Nikhil Gupta 4. Gaurav Gupta Sons of Late Sh. Sushil Gupta All R/o A-19/4, Rana Pratap Bagh, Delhi-110007 J U D G M E N (Suit for recovery of Rs.3,60,000/-) 1. Date of institution : 10.10.2012 2. Date of Final Order : 02.05.2018 3 . Final Order : Dismissed 1. Plaint 1.1.
texts.facts: 1. Plaint 1.1. Plaintiff has filed the present suit claiming to be the owner of Property bearing No.898-900, Gali To Novelty Cinema, S.P. Mukherji Marg, Delhi-110006, on the grounds that the Defendants who are in occupation of portion of the first floor and second floor of the said property as tenants for residential purposes alone, are using the said premises for storing heavy motor truck tyres, tubes, rims and other accessories related to the business of motor and truck tyres, tubes and rims etc, being run by them under the name CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. of M/s Rajasthan Trading Company, at 882 behind Novelty Cinema, S.P. Mukherji Marg, Delhi-110006. That the labours of the Defendants are also living and cooking in the said premises, because of which the walls and rooms of the premises have developed cracks and are getting damaged. Because of the aforesaid cooking by labours of the defendants in a place where tyres, tubes etc are being stored, there is also chance of fire in the building. 1.2. Accordingly, the Plaintiff has claimed damages @ Rs.10,000/- per month for the three years preceding to the filing of the suit i.e. total Rs.3,60,000/- and Plaintiff has also prayed for Mandatory Injunction so as to direct the Defendants to remove all the stored tyres, tubes etc from the tenanted premises and Ved Prakash vs Vijay Laxmi on 2 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59662408/ 1 also to stop labours from using the said premises from living and cooking. 2. WRITTEN STATEMENT 2.1. In the Written Statement, the Defendants admitted that they were paying rent to the Plaintiff and submitted that the property was let out by Sh.Raghunath Prasad in the year 1971 to the Father-in-law of Defendant No.1 and Grand- Father of Defendant No.2 to 4. They submitted that the premises was let out for residential-cum-commercial purposes and alleged that the rent receipts on which the Plaintiff has relied upon to prove the nature of tenancy is manipulated. As regards, storage of tyres, tubes, rims in the tenanted premises, the Defendants submitted that the tenanted premises was occupied by the Defendants as well as by their CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. servants to look after the goods stored there, as the tenanted premises was taken on rent for the purpose of storing the tyres and other goods as well as for the residence of the Defendants. They further submitted that the Defendants are cooking their food far away from the place where the tyres are stored and they are taking all security measures to prevent any untoward incident. They denied that the property has got damaged because of storage of articles by the Defendants. They submitted that the Plaintiff himself is using the remaining portion of the building for storing heavy cartoons and heavy bags of medicines etc and he is neither carrying out repairs nor permitting the Defendant to carry out repairs in the said property. Lastly, they prayed for dismissal of the suit. 3. In Replication to the Written Statement, the Plaintiff has denied the averments made by the Defendant and reiterated the contents of the Plaint. Hence the present suit is not maintainable." a) Relief of Mandatory injunction 130/- CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. 5.4. As per the aforesaid paragraph, the Plaintiff has valued the suit for purpose of damages @ Rs.3,60,000/- and for the relief of Mandatory Injunction @ Rs.130/-. 5.5. As per Section-7(i) of Court Fees Act, 1917, the amount of the fee payable in a suit for money, including suit for damages and compensation, shall be computed according to the amount claimed. In the present case, the Plaintiff has claimed damages of Rs.3,60,000/- and has valued the suit @ Rs.3,60,000/- for the said damages, therefore, the suit is correctly valued by the Plaintiff for the relief of damages. 5.6. As far as relief of Mandatory Injunction is concerned, as per Section-7(iv)(d) of the Court Fees Act r/w Punjab Amendment Act 26 of 1949, the value of such suit for the purpose of Court Fees is ad valorem on the amount of relief sought as valued and stated in the Plaint by the Plaintiff, provided that minimum court fees of Rs.13/- has to be paid. In the present case, the Plaintiff has valued the relief of Mandatory Injunction @ Rs.130/- and has paid the minimum court fees of Rs.13/- upon the same. 5.7 . In the opinion of the court, the suit is properly valued and court fees has been paid accordingly, Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the Plaintiff and against the Defendants. The onus to prove this issue is upon the Defendants and the Defendants in this regard in their Written Submissions have submitted as under :- CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash vs Vijay Laxmi on 2 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59662408/ 3 "It is submitted that in order to put illegal pressure upon the defendants either to vacate the tenanted portions or to increase the rent as per the wishes of landlord or to purchase the same , the plaintiff has filed two eviction petitions and the present suit. The eviction petitions were dismissed by the learned ARC and appeal against the same is pending. So the jurisdiction of this Hon'ble court is barred under the provisions of Delhi Rent Control Act." 6.2. As per Section-50 of Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, a civil court shall not entertain any suit or proceeding in so far as it relates to the fixation of standard rent in relation to any premises to which the Act applies or to eviction of any tenant therefrom or to any other matter which the Controller is empowered by or under the Act to decide and no Injunction in respect of any action taken or to be taken by the Controller under the said Act shall be granted by any civil court. In the present suit, the Plaintiff has sought damages from the Defendants for causing damages to the tenanted premises and there is no provision under Delhi Rent Control Act, under which damages can be awarded by the Controller to the landlord for the damages caused to the tenanted premises by the Tenant. OPP 7.1. The Plaintiff has sought two reliefs in the present suit :- a) Damages @ Rs.10,000/- per month for last three years (total Rs.3,60,000/-). b) Injunction to direct Defendants to remove the goods stored by them in the premises and to stop using the premises for residence for their labour. 7.2. The damages have been claimed by the Plaintiff for the damages caused to the property because of storage of goods by the Defendants in the said premises. It is stated in Para-7 of the Plaint that as the tenanted premises has been filled to capacity with goods like tyres, tubes, rims etc, hence the walls, floor as well as roof of the tenanted premises has got damaged and cracks have appeared therein. The very first fact that the Plaintiff was required to prove, was that actual damage was caused to building / tenanted premises, beyond normal wear and tear.
texts.arguments: 7.7. To prove the said fact, Plaintiff testified as PW-1 and in his Affidavit he reproduced the contents of Plaint and stated in Para-8 as under :- "Defendants started using the tenanted premises on the first and second floor let for residence only for storing heavy motor trucks tyres, tubes, rims and other accessories in bulk and keep the portion packed to the maximum of their capacity and as a consequence thereof the walls, floors, roofs of the tenanted premises have gone damaged by appearing cracks therein and are getting damaged for their day to day .............. The damage cause to the property has been seen by the Deponent with his own eyes". 7.8. The Plaintiff could not be cross-examined as he expired before he could be cross-examined, but even if his testimony is taken to be true, still the same is bereft of the description of damage, kind of damage, extent / nature of damage that has CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. been caused to the building. The Plaintiff cannot win the case by merely saying that damage is caused to my property hence pay me Rs.10,000/- per month. 7.9. PW-2 is Pramod Kumar Goel (son of deceased Plaintiff) and he too in his Affidavit, in Para-8, deposed verbatim the same as testified by his father / deceased Plaintiff (as reproduced above). 7.10. In his cross-examination, the witness admitted that there is no basis of claiming Rs.10,000/- as damages in follo words :- "I have not disclosed any basis of claiming Rs.10,000/- as damages per month from Defendants nor have filed any Ved Prakash vs Vijay Laxmi on 2 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59662408/ 5 valuation report." 7.11. He also admitted "We did not file any complaint before any authority for damage caused to suit property by defendant". 7.12. Thus, this witness admitted that there was no basis for claiming damage @ Rs.10,000/- per month for any damage caused to building and like PW-1 he also failed to prove the kind / nature of damage that the suit property suffered due to storage of alleged articles by the Defendants. 7.13. PW-3 Ved Prakash Kasana has tendered his Affidavit as Ex.PW3/A. In his affidavit he has not mentioned about any damage to the suit property but in last Para of Affidavit (i.e. Para-5) he testified as under :- "That, whenever the deponent visited the suit property, the deponent found the family of the defendants residing therein and no commercial activity or storage of tyres etc in CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. He also testified that the plaintiffs have stored tyres, tubes and rims etc. in the suit premises and that labour of the defendants are living in the tenanted premises and also cooking food there. 7.16. Moreover, his testimony is of no help to prove the fact that the damage caused to the suit property can be repaired and that such repair would entail cost of Rs.10,000/- per month or Rs.3,60,000/- in total. 7.18. In defence evidence, defendant No.2 Chetan Gupta testified as DW-1 and in his affidavit Ex. DW 1/A, he testified that the present suit has been filed by plaintiff only to pressurize the Ved Prakash vs Vijay Laxmi on 2 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59662408/ 6 defendants to vacate the suit property. That eviction petition filed by plaintiff were dismissed by Ld. ARC and that the suit is not maintainable as the plaintiff himself is responsible for neglecting the tenanted premises as he is neither maintaining the tenanted premises properly nor allowing the defendants to carry out necessary repairs. 7.19. DW-1 further deposed that the suit property was let out for residential-cum-commercial purposes. affidavit the witness stated that the tenanted premises is occupied by defendants as well as by their servants, who look after the goods stored there, as the tenanted premises was taken on rent for purpose of storing tyres and other goods as well as for residence of defendants. 7.20 . On the other hand, the respondents have averred that the tenanted premises was let out for composite purpose and the respondents are using some portions of the tenanted premises for commercial purposes and remaining portion for residential purposes for themselves and their servants. The petitioners have also sought to prove that the tenanted premises was let out solely for residential purposes by virtue of rent receipt wherein the word "RIHAISH" has been mentioned.
